newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Ousted Lesotho police chief told to return to work.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Lesotho police chief told to return to work.

text.p: Senior Lesotho police meeting on Monday declared full support for police commissioner Major General Bolutu Makoaba, who was ousted from his post last week by mutinous officers.

Eight members of the Royal Lesotho Mounted Police seized control of police headquarters last Thursday and claimed to dismiss Makoaba, who was out of the country on an official visit to Nambia, and two other officers.

The group, resisting arrest for the killings of three fellow officers in 1995, are claiming amnesty under Lesotho's Pardons Act, which stipulates that security force members may not be charged for any crimes committed between 1993 and 1995.

"Lesotho should not degenerate into anarchy nor be turned into a 'banana republic' where law and order do not exist for the sake of sectional and myopic interests," a statement released after Monday's meeting said.
"No illegal appointments will enjoy the support of any kind from senior officers," it added.
It also said all dismissed officers should immediately return to work and resume normal duties, but did not say how the issue of the mutineers would be resolved.
Western diplomats said the mutiny had not disrupted day-to-day life in the mountainous Southern African kingdom's capital.
